newsitem.title: USA: Stewart & Stevenson sees lower Q3 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Stewart & Stevenson sees lower Q3 EPS.

text.p: Stewart & Stevenson Services Inc said on Monday it anticipated lower-than-expected third quarter earnings, because most of its new orders in the past six months were not for manufacture until 1997.

The company said it expected to earn between $0.20 and $0.24 per share in the third quarter, compared with analyst estimates of about $0.36 per share. Most new orders were not recognized as sales during the most recent quarters, it said.

Stewart & Stevenson, which makes diesel and gas turbine powered equipment, said it received two orders totalling $45 million for three gas turbine operators during October, bringing orders in the third quarter to $121 million.
"The level of new orders is very encouraging and should produce higher turbine sales in the future," the company said.
Chief Executive Officer Robert Hargrave said recent improvements in this market should ensure favorable earnings comparison as the company entered 1997.
Net orders for the past two quarters were about $220 million compared to $51 million for the same period last year, the company said.
In addition, the company signed a seven-year lease with a South American utility to provide one LM2500 gas turbine generator, the company said.
